card_summary: What NAD+ actually does, why researchers are interested in how its levels change with age, and what we still don't know about a nasal spray.
kicker: Energy Spray Rx · How it works
headline: The molecule that keeps your cells' *power line* moving.
lede: NAD+ isn't a peptide and it isn't a stimulant. It's a working part inside every cell, and research suggests you have less of it as you age. Here's what it does, what the evidence says, and where the real questions are.
dose_spray_pattern: 1 to 2 sprays once daily on weekdays, two months on and one month off
recognition: The second coffee used to be optional. A hard week used to take a weekend to shake off, not the whole next week. When energy shifts like that, it's natural to wonder what's changing underneath.
reframe: NAD+ is a molecule your cells use to turn food into usable energy. Researchers are interested in it for two reasons: levels appear to fall with age, and it's now possible to raise them. Whether raising them changes how you feel day to day is still the open question.
viz_intro: Mitochondria turn the food you eat into energy your cells can spend. NAD+ is the shuttle that keeps that line moving.
viz_alt: A mitochondrion with gold dots circling inside it. On the left, NAD+ picks up electrons from broken-down food. On the right, it drops them off to make cellular energy, then loops back.
viz_molecule_label: Gold dots: NAD+ on its loop

viz_nodes.node_detail: As your cells break down sugar and fat, NAD+ collects electrons and becomes NADH. Think of it as a delivery truck being loaded.
NADH hands those electrons to the mitochondria's energy chain, which makes ATP, the energy every cell spends. Then it's NAD+ again and ready for another trip.
Other enzymes, including sirtuins, PARPs and CD38, use NAD+ up for jobs like DNA maintenance. Your cells have to keep rebuilding their supply.

viz_caption: Simplified. Your cells run this loop constantly, in every mitochondrion.
viz_tap_hint: Tap a plum dot for detail.
gauge_title: NAD+ in human skin, younger vs. older

gauge_states.state_note: Skin samples from younger people had higher NAD+.
Skin samples from older people had lower NAD+, in women and men alike. It's one study of 49 people, and few human studies have measured this, so read it as an early clue rather than the final word.

gauge_scale_note: Bars show direction, not measured amounts.
mechanism_title: What we know, and what we don't
mechanism_intro: Four ideas, each with a different level of certainty.

mechanism_steps.step_title: It's a shuttle, not a stimulant
mechanism_steps.step_body: NAD+ carries electrons from the food you break down to the machinery that makes cellular energy. It's part of the basic equipment in every cell, the way a delivery truck is part of a supply chain.

mechanism_steps.step_title: Levels appear to drop with age
mechanism_steps.step_body: In skin samples from 49 people, newborns and adults aged 15 to 77, NAD+ was lower in older skin, in women and men. Only a handful of human studies have measured this directly.
In mice, an enzyme called CD38 that uses up NAD+ rises with age and accounts for much of the decline. Whether the same holds in people is still being worked out.

mechanism_steps.step_title: Raising it is possible. Feeling different is the open question.
mechanism_steps.step_body: Small human trials show that oral NAD+ building blocks can raise NAD+ in the blood. A 2025 review found that measurable benefits in people have been limited so far.

notice_intro: There's less human data here than for most of what we offer. This is what's known, stated plainly.

notice_items.notice_text: Studies of oral NAD+ building blocks, a different form from a nasal spray, ran for weeks: for example, 6 weeks in one trial of 30 adults. There are no human studies of nasal NAD+ yet, so your clinician will set expectations with you.
Nasal NAD+ hasn't been studied in people yet. Tell your clinician about anything new, including nasal discomfort, headache or sleep changes.

route_intro: A nasal spray, on a schedule your clinician sets.
route_figure_label: Figure showing a nasal spray route from the nose, with a dotted path to the brain.

route_steps.route_text: Each bottle holds {{dose_concentration}} NAD+ in a water-based spray. Use it within about 35 days of opening.
There are no published human studies of nasal NAD+ yet. In a rat study, NAD+ given through the nose raised NAD+ levels in the brain.

cautions_intro: Your clinician screens your health history and medications during intake. Here's what the evidence can and can't tell you so far.

not_for_you_if.item_text: Your clinician will set this list with you. Published human data for nasal NAD+ don't yet define who should avoid it.

what_to_watch.item_text: In one small study of NAD+ given by IV drip, a different route and a much larger dose, people reported stomach upset, a faster heart rate and chest pressure during the drip, which stopped once it ended. Nasal sprays haven't been studied this way. Tell your clinician about anything new.
Any nasal irritation, headache or change in sleep after you start.
